subject: Business Models
title: The Silk Road
description: A quick, practical guide to The Silk Road.

hook.text: A 4,000-mile trade network connected China to Rome. Silk, spices, and ideas flowed for centuries.

buildup.text: No single merchant traveled the entire route. Goods passed through dozens of middlemen and markets.

discovery.text: Each middleman added a markup. Chinese silk costing 1 coin in Xi'an sold for 100 in Rome.

twist.text: The road also spread diseases. The Black Death likely traveled from Asia to Europe along trade routes.

climax.text: The Silk Road proved that commerce connects civilizations—for better and for worse.

punchline.text: 4,000 miles of markup. Global trade started with camels.

quiz.question: How did goods move along the Silk Road?

details.summary: The Silk Road was a 4,000-mile network of trade routes connecting China to the Mediterranean from the 2nd century BCE to the 15th century CE..
details.whyItMatters: The Silk Road was the first global supply chain, demonstrating how trade creates interdependence between distant civilizations..
takeaways: A 4,000-mile trade network connected China to Rome for over 1,500 years
Goods traveled through chains of intermediary traders, not end-to-end journeys
The Silk Road transmitted religion, technology, and disease alongside trade goods

faq.question: How did goods actually travel along the Silk Road?
faq.answer: Few traders traveled the entire route. Instead, goods passed through chains of intermediaries at oasis trading cities like Samarkand and Bukhara. Each merchant controlled a segment, buying goods from one direction and selling to traders heading the other way..

faq.question: Why did the Silk Road decline?
faq.answer: Ottoman Empire expansion raised transit costs and taxes. Maritime trade routes pioneered by Portuguese explorers offered cheaper, faster alternatives. The fall of the Mongol Empire fragmented the political stability that protected overland trade. European demand shifted to sea-accessible goods.
